source_en: Graphite, a crystalline allotrope of carbon (mineral carbon), triturated for homeopathic use.
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for eczema with sticky, honey-like oozing and cracked skin.
Used for fissures of the nipples, anus and toes.
Described for chilly, stout, constipated constitutions.
Said to suit delayed or scanty menses.
safety_note: Graphite dust can irritate eyes, skin and airways and long exposure may cause lung disease; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Crude petroleum (rock oil), a hydrocarbon mixture, potentised from the refined/crude oil.
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for cracked, rough skin and eczema worse in winter.
Used for travel and motion sickness, nausea worse in vehicles or ships.
Described for morning diarrhoea and heartburn.
Said to suit dry, deep coughs and hoarseness worse in cold air.
typical_potency_dosage: 3C to 30C (Boericke lists 3rd to 30th, noting low doses often work better).
safety_note: Crude petroleum contains hydrocarbons, some carcinogenic, and is harmful if swallowed or inhaled; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Pure silica (silicon dioxide, flint/quartz), prepared by trituration to make it soluble.
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for slow-healing suppuration, boils and abscesses.
Used for chilly, weak, oversensitive constitutions with poor nutrition.
Described for brittle nails and slow-growing tissue.
Said to help expel foreign bodies and soften scar tissue.
typical_potency_dosage: 6C to 30C; higher (200C) cited in some sources (Boericke gives ~6x to 30x).
safety_note: Inhaled crystalline silica dust causes silicosis and lung disease, but this concerns industrial exposure, not dilutions; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Sundew, Drosera rotundifolia (family Droseraceae), whole fresh plant.
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for spasmodic, dry, barking coughs resembling whooping cough.
Used for coughing fits with vomiting, worse after midnight.
Described for hoarseness and a scraping throat.
Said to suit cough worse when lying down or after laughing or talking.
typical_potency_dosage: 1x to 12x tincture/dilution per Boericke; 30C in common practice.
safety_note: No well-documented acute toxicity in the sources I read; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Eyebright, Euphrasia officinalis (Euphrasia genus, family Orobanchaceae; formerly Scrophulariaceae), whole plant.
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for profuse, burning, watery eye discharge with a bland nasal discharge.
Used for red, irritated eyes worse in light and wind.
Described for early measles or colds with marked eye symptoms.
Said to suit conjunctival irritation after exposure.
typical_potency_dosage: 3C to 6C (Boericke lists 3rd to 6th); tincture also used for eyewash historically.
safety_note: Efficacy of eyebright eye preparations is undocumented per the EMA; non-sterile eyewashes may cause infection; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Marsh Labrador tea, Rhododendron tomentosum (syn. Ledum palustre; family Ericaceae), plant.
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for puncture wounds and insect bites, cold to touch and relieved by cold.
Used for rheumatic pains ascending from feet, better from cold applications.
Described for black eyes and bruising.
Said to suit poison-ivy-like eruptions.
typical_potency_dosage: 3C to 30C (Boericke lists 3rd to 30th); 30C or 200C for injuries.
safety_note: Plant terpenes (ledol, grayanotoxins) can cause dizziness, spasms, nausea and unconsciousness in overdose; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Mayapple, Podophyllum peltatum (family Berberidaceae), rhizome/root.
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for profuse, gushing, offensive morning diarrhoea.
Used for liver and gallbladder complaints with rumbling of the abdomen.
Described for diarrhoea during teething in children.
Said to suit prolapse of rectum or uterus with straining.
safety_note: All parts of the plant are poisonous; podophyllin is a strong purgative and podophyllotoxin is toxic; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Pokeroot, Phytolacca americana/decandra (family Phytolaccaceae), fresh root.
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for sore throat with dark red tonsils and pain radiating to the ears.
Used for hard, painful, swollen glands and mastitis.
Described for rheumatic and shooting bone pains worse in damp weather.
Said to suit breast pain when nursing.
typical_potency_dosage: Mother tincture to 3x per Boericke; 30C commonly cited elsewhere.
safety_note: Poke is toxic in all parts, especially root and unripe berries; mother tincture can be hazardous; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Seeds of Schoenocaulon officinale (family Melanthiaceae), also called cevadilla (not confirmed on source page).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for hay-fever-like sneezing with watery nose and eyes.
Used for sore throat with a lump sensation, better from warm drinks.
Described for chilly, easily startled people with imaginary-illness ideas.
Said to suit worm complaints with reflex symptoms.
safety_note: Seeds are highly toxic (veratridine, cevadine alkaloids) and used as insecticide; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Seeds of stavesacre, Delphinium staphisagria (family Ranunculaceae).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for suppressed anger, indignation and humiliation.
Used for cystitis-like urinary irritation, including after intimacy ('honeymoon cystitis').
Described for itchy eczema with crusts and styes.
Said to suit pain and wounds after surgery or clean cuts.
safety_note: All parts are highly toxic; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Valerian root, Valeriana officinalis (family Caprifoliaceae, formerly Valerianaceae).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for nervous excitability, sleeplessness and hysteria-type states.
Used for oversensitivity to pain and noise.
Described for cramping pains in the legs at night.
Said to suit restless states in sensitive women and children.
safety_note: Valerian is a CNS depressant, avoid with alcohol or sedatives; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this. Herbal valerian (not homeopathic) has mixed evidence for sleep, with EMA recognizing it for mild nervous tension.

source_en: Seed oil of Croton tiglium (family Euphorbiaceae), purging croton.
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for sudden, yellow, gushing diarrhoea after eating or drinking.
Used for intensely itchy, vesicular eczema, especially on genitals, worse on touch.
Described for skin eruptions that alternate with diarrhoea.
Said to suit shooting pains from the nipple to the back when nursing.
safety_note: Seeds are highly toxic and a severe purgative; croton oil is a skin irritant and co-carcinogen; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Seed of nutmeg, Myristica fragrans (family Myristicaceae).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for drowsiness, fainting and a dreamy, dazed state.
Used for extreme dryness of mouth with no thirst.
Described for bloating and gas after eating.
Said to suit changeable moods, laughing and crying.
safety_note: Large nutmeg doses cause delirium, palpitations, convulsions and psychosis; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Seed (horse chestnut) of Aesculus hippocastanum (family Sapindaceae).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for painful, purplish haemorrhoids with a sensation of sticks in the rectum.
Used for aching low back and sacral pain on walking.
Described for venous congestion and varicose veins.
Said to suit dry, burning, raw throat.
typical_potency_dosage: Mother tincture to 3x per Boericke; 6C to 30C common.
safety_note: Raw seeds are toxic (aesculin, saponins); tincture can be hazardous; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this. Standardised horse chestnut seed extract (not homeopathy) showed short-term benefit in chronic venous insufficiency in a 2012 Cochrane review of low-quality trials.

source_en: Berries of chaste tree, Vitex agnus-castus (family Lamiaceae).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for low sexual desire and impotence with a sense of melancholy.
Used for scanty milk in nursing mothers.
Described for premature ageing of the sexual functions.
Said to suit irregular menses and PMS complaints.
safety_note: Herbal vitex may cause GI upset and headache and is discouraged in pregnancy and with hormonal or dopamine-related drugs; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this. Herbal chasteberry has little high-quality clinical evidence for PMS.

source_en: Leaf (and oil) of Eucalyptus globulus, blue gum (family Myrtaceae).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for catarrh with profuse thick discharge.
Used for bronchitis and moist asthma in the elderly.
Described for sore, ulcerated throat and tonsils.
Said to suit intermittent fevers and slow digestion.
typical_potency_dosage: Tincture 1 to 20 drops or lower potencies per Boericke; oil 5 drops.
safety_note: Eucalyptus oil is toxic if swallowed, particularly in children; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Water hemlock / cowbane, Cicuta virosa (family Apiaceae), root.
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for violent convulsions with rigidity and distortion.
Used for after-effects of head injury with spasms.
Described for childish behaviour and staring.
Said to suit eruptions with thick yellow crusts on the face.
safety_note: Cicutoxin makes the plant among the most toxic, often fatal in small amounts; mother tincture and low potencies are dangerous; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Gumweed, Grindelia robusta/squarrosa (family Asteraceae).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for asthma with difficulty breathing on lying down or falling asleep.
Used for thick, tenacious mucus hard to expectorate.
Described for poison-oak-type skin reactions and blisters.
Said to suit pain in the spleen region.
typical_potency_dosage: Tincture 1 to 15 drops or lower potencies per Boericke.
safety_note: Gumweed resin can irritate; avoid mother tincture without guidance; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Small stinging nettle, Urtica urens (family Urticaceae).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for burning, stinging hives and nettle rash.
Used for gouty and uric-acid complaints.
Described for minor burns and scalds.
Said to suit low milk supply in nursing mothers.
typical_potency_dosage: Tincture or low potencies per Boericke; 30C elsewhere.
safety_note: Fresh plant causes stinging skin irritation; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Wild pansy, Viola tricolor (family Violaceae).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for milk crust and eczema of the scalp and face in children.
Used for impetigo with thick, cracking crusts.
Described for strong-smelling urine like cat urine.
Said to suit skin complaints worse in winter.
safety_note: Low toxicity; seeds/roots are an emetic and laxative; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Comfrey, Symphytum officinale (family Boraginaceae), root.
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for fractures slow to heal.
Used for pain at the fracture site and periosteum.
Described for blunt injuries to the eyeball.
Said to suit irritable stumps after amputation.
safety_note: Comfrey contains hepatotoxic pyrrolizidine alkaloids; FDA banned internal-use products; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Fly agaric mushroom, Amanita muscaria (family Amanitaceae).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for twitching, tremors and chorea-like jerking.
Used for burning-itching chilblains worse in cold.
Described for sensitivity of the spine and trembling.
Said to suit people sensitive to cold and open air.
safety_note: Contains muscimol and ibotenic acid, causing delirium and hallucinations; fatalities rare; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Magnesium carbonate (MgCO3, mineral magnesite).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for sour smell and sour stools in infants.
Used for toothache and neuralgia in tired, worn women.
Described for sleeplessness with unrefreshing sleep.
Said to suit facial pains worse at night.
safety_note: Low toxicity; may be a laxative in large amounts. Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Animal charcoal, charred animal material (bone-char type, with calcium phosphate and carbon).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for indurated, hardened glands.
Used for venous stagnation and bluish skin.
Described for old, foul, spongy ulcers.
Said to suit debility after exhausting illness.
safety_note: Low toxicity; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.

source_en: Root of Smilax species (e.g. Smilax ornata), sarsaparilla (family Smilacaceae).
keynotes_en: Traditionally indicated for severe pain at the end of urination, with gravel.
Used for dry, cracked skin and eruptions on the face.
Described for burning urine in children who scream.
Said to suit eruptions that are worse in spring.
safety_note: Low toxicity at usual doses; Homeopathic dilutions above roughly 12C are ultra-dilute; mother tinctures and very low potencies of toxic substances can be hazardous.
evidence_note: Systematic reviews (e.g. Cochrane 2010, Australian NHMRC 2015) find no reliable evidence that homeopathy works beyond placebo; no remedy-specific trials found that change this.
